text:
maria: heads up — saw a recurring p95 token latency spike on /chat (hosted) across yesterday evening. digging into token-level breakdown now, but kv/prefix cache numbers look weird :thinking_face:

sam: on it. do you have a short query or screenshot? any pattern by route or model variant?

maria: I pulled a quick PromQL slice: `sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_lookups_total[5m]))` by (route) — hit rate for /chat-v2 drops from ~0.82 -> 0.46 during spikes. evictions up too: `increase(kv_cache_evictions_total[15m])` shows bursts synced with higher request load.

chris: that aligns with the profiler dump I grabbed at 18:12. kernel selection kept flipping between `kern_v1` and `kern_v2` for tokens past 1024 seq. lots of short-lived batches forming (~4-8 reqs) so amortization is bad.

devon: can you paste the profiler stack? even a small snippet helps. also curious if prefix cache reuse per-route is reported anywhere.

maria: pasted minimal excerpt below (from perf-bundle):
```
# profile 2025-07-24 18:12
cpu: kernel_selector.chooseKernel  42%
cpu: batcher.makeBatch          23%
cpu: kv_cache.lookup            12%
cpu: kv_cache.evict             8%
cpu: tokenizer.decode           5%
```

maria: the kv_cache.lookup spike correlates with the p95 token latency. notice the evict line too.

sam: interesting. I also saw a change in batching heuristics after the last deploy — the batcher now prefers sub-100ms spin wait before dispatch to improve latency for single-turn flows. might cause small batch size under bursty traffic.

chris: that heuristic helped tail for single-user flows but kills throughput for bursty /chat where many routes share same model but different prefixes. if cache thrash occurs we lose KV reuse across requests.

devon: we should add route-scoped cache metrics: `kv_cache.hit_rate{route}`, `kv_cache.evictions{route}`, `kv_cache.memory_bytes{route}`, and `prefix_cache.reuse_count{route}`. also emit `token_latency.*` breakdown per route: `token_latency.kv_lookup_ms`, `token_latency.kernel_exec_ms`, `token_latency.decode_ms`, `token_latency.queue_ms`.

sam: +1. I prototyped a Grafana layout: a single dashboard with rows: 1) global hit_rate / evictions / mem, 2) per-route sparklines for hit_rate + evictions, 3) per-route token-level stacked bars (kv/kernel/decode/queue), 4) kernel-selector flip rate.

maria: can you paste the PromQLs you used? I'll pair with infra to add alerts. We need an alert when route hit_rate < 0.6 and evictions rate > threshold.

sam: sure — snippets: 
- Route hit rate: `sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) by (route) / sum(rate(kv_cache_lookups_total[5m])) by (route)`
- Eviction rate: `sum(increase(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m])) by (route)`
- Memory footprint: `max_over_time(kv_cache_memory_bytes[10m]) by (route)`
- Per-token kv lookup latency: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_kv_lookup_bucket[5m])) by (le,route))`
- Kernel flip rate: `sum(rate(kernel_selector_flips_total[5m])) by (model_variant)`

chris: also add an aggregate metric `cache_reuse_score{route}` = `kv_hits / (kv_lookups + evictions)` to highlight thrash.

devon: operationally we might shard prefix cache by route affinity so hot prefixes don't evict each other. but first let's get visibility.

maria: action items: 1) sam -> add Grafana panels + PromQL (ETA end of day) 2) infra -> add alert: route hit_rate < 0.6 for 10m & evictions > 100/5m 3) eng-runtime -> explore batcher knob rollback (reduce spin-wait) + measure impact 4) perf -> collect 30m of profiles during peak and upload to perf-bucket.

sam: I'll start dashboard and create a temp alert rule in staging. posting links when done.

perf-bot: reminder: perf summary job for /chat-v2 scheduled at 2025-07-25T02:00Z. upload path: s3://redwood-perf/chats/v2/2025-07-25/

maria: thanks all. let's reconvene tomorrow 10am PT if dashboards / alerts catch the spike. :thumbsup:
